x: A is incorrect: Article 48A is about protecting and improving the environment, forests and wildlife; separation of the judiciary from the executive is Article 50. Articles 44 (UCC) and 39A (free legal aid) are stated correctly.
t: Check the Article number against its subject.

x: Both are true and R explains A: courts cannot enforce the Directive Principles because Article 37 declares them non-justiciable, though fundamental in governance.
t: Check whether R is the provision behind A.

x: Both are true: Article 37 calls DPSP fundamental in governance, and since courts cannot enforce them, their sanction is moral and political (public opinion and elections).
t: Contrast the legal sanction of rights with the political sanction of DPSP.

x: All four are correct: the 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A and 48A; the 44th widened Article 38 to minimise inequalities; the 86th recast Article 45 for children below six; the 97th added Article 43B on co-operatives.
t: Match each amendment to the DPSP Article it changed.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding amendments related to the Directive Principles:
I. The 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A and 48A.
II. The 44th Amendment made Article 38 more comprehensive by including the objective of minimising inequalities.
III. The 86th Amendment changed Article 45 to deal with education for children below six years.
IV. The 97th Amendment added Article 43B relating to cooperative societies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: 42nd (1976), 44th (1978), 86th (2002), 97th (2011): A, B, C, D — amendment numbers rise with the years.
t: Higher amendment numbers come later.

x: Four: Articles 40 (village panchayats), 43B (co-operatives), 46 (weaker sections) and 48 (cattle) are Gandhian. Article 44 (UCC) and 50 (separation of judiciary) are liberal-intellectual principles.
t: Sort each Article into Gandhian or liberal-intellectual.

x: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) – Fundamental Rights above DPSP; Golaknath (1967) – Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) – basic structure; Minerva Mills (1980) – balance between FRs and DPSP.
t: Order the cases by year and follow the shift in doctrine.

x: Both are true: DPSP were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim at a welfare state.
t: Recall the source and goal of DPSP.

x: Article 38 – welfare of the people; 39 – livelihood, equal pay, protection of children; 41 – right to work, education and public assistance; 42 – humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
t: Match each DPSP Article to its welfare goal.

x: C is incorrect: Article 43A provides for workers' participation in the management of industries, not agriculture. Articles 43 (living wage) and 47 (nutrition, public health) are stated correctly.
t: Watch for one word changed in a provision.

x: Article 43 – cottage industries (with living wage); 46 – educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections; 47 – prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs; 48 – ban on slaughter of cows and milch animals.
t: Match each Gandhian Article to its directive.

x: Article 45 – originally free education up to 14; 48 – agriculture and animal husbandry; 48A – forests and wildlife; 49 – monuments of national importance.
t: Separate 48 (agriculture) from 48A (environment).

x: Both are true: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and aim at political democracy; DPSP aim at social and economic democracy.
t: Contrast the aims of the two Parts.

x: Champakam Dorairajan (1951), Golaknath (1967), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), Minerva Mills (1980): B, D, C, A.
t: Order the cases by year.

x: DPSP are called the 'Instrument of Instructions' (like those under the 1935 Act) and the 'conscience of the Constitution' (Granville Austin).
t: Recall the two names for DPSP.

x: Protecting the environment is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(g). Article 48A makes it a Directive Principle, not a duty.
t: Separate the duty (51A(g)) from the directive (48A).

x: Fundamental Rights carry a legal sanction because courts enforce them. 'Moral and political' sanction and 'fundamental in governance' describe DPSP.
t: Contrast legal sanction (FR) with moral sanction (DPSP).

x: DPSP are in Part IV, Articles 36 to 51. Part III (12–35) is Fundamental Rights and Part IVA (Article 51A) Fundamental Duties.
t: Link DPSP to Part IV.

x: C is incorrect: Article 43B (co-operative societies) was added by the 97th Amendment (2011), not the 42nd. The others are right: Article 40 panchayats, 50 separation of judiciary, 46 weaker sections.
t: Check which amendment added each 'A/B' Article.

x: Article 40 – village panchayats; 47 – nutrition, standard of living, prohibition; 50 – separation of judiciary from executive; 51 – international peace and security.
t: Match each Article to its subject.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the aims of DPSP (social and economic democracy, welfare state) do not explain why they were borrowed from Ireland.
t: The purpose of a provision does not explain its source.

x: The socialistic principles make up about 8–9 Articles of Part IV (38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A, 47).
t: Count the socialistic Articles.

x: All eight listed — Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A and 47 — are key socialistic principles.
t: Check each Article against the socialistic group.

x: All six — Articles 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47 and 48 — are Gandhian principles. Articles 43 and 47 appear in both the socialistic and Gandhian lists.
t: Note the Articles shared between groups.

x: Both are true: the liberal-intellectual group has seven Articles, including 44 (UCC), 45 (early childhood care), 48 (agriculture) and 48A (environment).
t: Recall the liberal-intellectual Articles.

x: Article 36 defines 'State' for Part IV (as Article 12 does for Part III). Article 37 makes DPSP non-justiciable; 38 and 39 set the welfare and policy goals.
t: Link Article 36 to the definition of 'State'.

x: Both are true: Article 38 seeks a just social order and minimised inequalities; Article 39 lists principles on livelihood, equal pay and protection of children.
t: Recall Articles 38 and 39.

x: Article 39A – equal justice and free legal aid; 41 – right to work, education, public assistance; 42 – humane work conditions and maternity relief; 43 – living wage and cottage industries.
t: Match each Article to its welfare goal.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Article 43B (co-operatives) is a separate directive and does not explain Article 43A (workers' participation in management).
t: Neighbouring Articles do not explain each other.

x: All three are correct: Article 44 – Uniform Civil Code; 45 – early childhood care and education; 48 – agriculture, animal husbandry and ban on cow slaughter.
t: Check each Article against its subject.

x: All three are correct: Articles 49 (monuments), 50 (separation of judiciary) and 51 (international peace) are liberal-intellectual principles.
t: Recall the last Articles of Part IV as liberal-intellectual.

x: All four are correct: Article 48A protects the environment, forests and wildlife, and Article 49 protects monuments.
t: Recall the subjects of 48A and 49.
Higher amendment numbers come in later years.
